evidence.observation: The default non-interactive runner (signature at line 42) has no timeout parameter and passes none to subprocess.Popen: the Popen call (lines 62-73) sets stdout=PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT (stderr merged into stdout), text=True, shell=True, errors='replace', bufsize=0 and cwd. Output is captured by a byte/char-at-a-time loop (lines 75-81) reading process.stdout.read(1); each chunk is echoed with print(..., flush=True) and also appended to a list. Exit status is taken after process.wait() and returned as process.returncode together with the joined output (line 84). Any exception during setup/execution is swallowed and turned into the tuple (1, str(e)) (lines 85-86). So: no timeout enforcement is present; a hung lint/run command blocks forever.

Public entry point. Chooses run_cmd_pexpect only when stdin is a TTY, pexpect.spawn exists and the platform is not Windows (line 13); otherwise it uses run_cmd_subprocess (line 16). It accepts no timeout argument, so callers cannot bound execution time. It catches OSError and returns the exit status 1 plus a formatted error message, either printed (default) or routed through error_print (lines 17-23).

Interactive path. Accumulates output into a BytesIO buffer via an output_callback passed to child.interact (lines 100-104, 124), then child.close() and returns (child.exitstatus, decoded buffer) (lines 127-128). There is no timeout argument to interact/close and no pexpect timeout configuration, so the interactive branch is likewise unbounded. pexpect/TypeError/ValueError failures are converted to (1, error_msg) (lines 130-132).

Linter.run_cmd appends the oslex-quoted relative filename to the raw command string (line 48) and delegates to run_cmd_subprocess from aider.run_cmd (imported line 15), passing cwd=self.root and encoding=self.encoding but no timeout (lines 53-57). It captures the returned (returncode, stdout) tuple and treats stdout as the lint 'errors' text even though run_cmd_subprocess merges stderr into it. Exit-status handling: a zero exit status short-circuits and returns None (lines 62-63) meaning no lint problems; a non-zero status wraps the output as '## Running: <cmd>' plus errors and converts it via errors_to_lint_result (lines 65-68). OSError (e.g. command not found) is caught and only printed (lines 58-60).

The built-in Python flake8 path does not use run_cmd_subprocess; it calls subprocess.run directly (line 151) with capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, encoding/errors settings and cwd (lines 151-159), and no timeout argument. Output capture combines both streams: errors = result.stdout + result.stderr (line 160). Exit status is deliberately not inspected (check=False); instead the code decides there are no errors when the combined text is empty (lines 164-165) and otherwise returns errors_to_lint_result (line 168). Exceptions are turned into an 'Error running flake8:' string instead of a nonzero status (lines 161-162).

Translates captured lint text into a LintResult: returns None for empty text (lines 71-72), extracts positive 1-based line numbers from '<filename>:<lineno>' matches against the current relative filename (lines 74-78), converts them to 0-based indices (line 78) and returns LintResult(text, lines) (line 80). This is how exit-status-derived lint output is mapped back onto source lines for the tree-context display in Linter.lint.

claims.claim: Neither aider/run_cmd.py nor the flake8 path in aider/linter.py imposes any timeout: run_cmd, run_cmd_subprocess and run_cmd_pexpect accept no timeout argument and never pass one to subprocess.Popen or pexpect, and flake8_lint calls subprocess.run without a timeout. Execution is therefore unbounded for a hung command.

Output capture in aider/run_cmd.py merges stderr into stdout (stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) in the subprocess path and accumulates the stream while echoing it live; the pexpect path buffers all bytes via an interact output_filter. Callers such as Linter.run_cmd receive the captured text as the second tuple element.

Exit-status handling differs by path: run_cmd_subprocess returns process.returncode after wait() (and 1 on any exception); run_cmd catches OSError and returns 1; run_cmd_pexpect returns child.exitstatus. Linter.run_cmd treats returncode == 0 as 'no lint errors' and returns None, otherwise it formats the captured output as lint results.

Linter.flake8_lint ignores the flake8 exit status entirely (check=False): it decides whether lint problems exist solely from whether the concatenated stdout+stderr text is non-empty, and converts subprocess startup exceptions into an error string rather than a status code.

The repository tests exercise these contracts: tests/basic/test_linter.py mocks subprocess.Popen to assert run_cmd returns None on a mocked returncode 0 and returns a populated LintResult on returncode 1, while tests/basic/test_run_cmd.py asserts run_cmd returns exit_code 0 and 'Hello, World!' for an echo command.

conclusion: aider/run_cmd.py exposes one public helper (run_cmd) that dispatches to either an interactive pexpect runner or a non-interactive subprocess runner. Both capture output, but stderr is merged into stdout in the subprocess path and full output is buffered (while also echoed live). Exit status is propagated as process.returncode (subprocess) or child.exitstatus (pexpect), with exceptions collapsed to status 1. Crucially, there is no timeout handling anywhere in run_cmd.py or in aider/linter.py: no timeout parameter, no subprocess timeout kwarg, no pexpect timeout, so a hanging lint or run command blocks indefinitely. aider/linter.py consumes run_cmd_subprocess output as lint text, maps a zero exit status to 'no errors' (returning None), and for non-zero status parses '<file>:<line>' occurrences into 0-based line indices for tree-context display; its flake8 path bypasses run_cmd_subprocess, uses subprocess.run(capture_output=True), concatenates stdout+stderr, and ignores returncode (check=False), inferring problems only from non-empty output.

validation.notes: The focused test suite for these two modules could not run: collection fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'oslex' (aider/linter.py:10) and No module named 'pexpect' (aider/run_cmd.py:7); 'grep_ast' is also unavailable. These are optional runtime dependencies that are not installed and I was instructed not to install dependencies. As a dependency-free substitute I ran a static check: `python -m py_compile aider/linter.py aider/run_cmd.py` succeeded, and an ast-based check confirmed every cited symbol (run_cmd, run_cmd_subprocess, run_cmd_pexpect, Linter.run_cmd, Linter.flake8_lint, Linter.errors_to_lint_result) exists and is fully contained in its cited inclusive line range.
